summary_en: A 125-micrometer acousto-optic sensor embedded in a 24-gauge needle stylet enables ultrasound-relative 3D needle-tip localization, imaging from within tissue at the needle tip, and relative temperature monitoring during ablation. Bench testing reported 1.4 mm mean in-plane localization error and a 2.1 cm median out-of-plane detection threshold. Ex-vivo and in-vivo experiments demonstrated tracking through ablation zones and sufficient internal imaging resolution to distinguish vessels and cystic versus solid structures. Because sensing hardware and image acquisition are central contributions, this is a core acoustic-optical imaging paper rather than merely a downstream clinical-analysis study.
